edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Σπουδάσατε οὖν μιᾷ εὐχαριστίᾳ χρῆσθαι: μία γὰρ σὰρξ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἓν ποτήριον εἰς ἕνωσιν τοῦ αἵματος αὐτοῦ, ἓν θυσιαστήριον, ὡς εἷς ἐπίσκοπος ἅμα τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ καὶ διακόνοις τοῖς συνδούλοις μου: ἵνα, ὃ ἐὰν πράσσητε, κατὰ θεὸν πράσσητε.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore be diligent to make use of a single Eucharist, because the flesh of our Lord Jesus Christ is one, and the cup for union with his blood is one, the altar is one, as the bishop is one together with the presbytery and the deacons who are my fellow slaves, in order that whatever you may do, you may do according to God.
pass_b_english: Be eager, then, to use one Eucharist, so that whatever you do, you do it God's way. For there is one flesh of our Lord Jesus Christ, and one cup for union with his blood. There is one altar, just as there is one bishop, with the presbytery and the deacons, my fellow slaves.

choices.why: χράομαι 'use, take part in'; εὐχαριστία here is the rite. 'Use' kept for the verb.

choices.english: one cup for union with his blood
choices.why: εἰς of purpose; the cup unites with his blood.
rejected: to show forth the unity of His blood

choices.why: Short and spoken; 'according to God' sounds foreign in reading text.

anf_compare.notes: Same sense. ANF supplies '[show forth]' and '[the will of]'; we render εἰς ἕνωσιν as purpose without supplements.

notes: One cup and one flesh may recall 1 Corinthians 10:16-17; not cited inline.
Source accent on συνδούλοις kept as supplied.
Repair 2026-10-02 per checker a: ἵνα clause rendered as purpose of 'use one Eucharist' (Greek order: σπουδάσατε… εὐχαριστίᾳ χρῆσθαι… ἵνα… πράσσητε), not a wish.

review.notes: Checked paragraph 1 only. «Σπουδάσατε οὖν μιᾷ εὐχαριστίᾳ χρῆσθαι» = A «Therefore be diligent to make use of a single Eucharist» / B «Be eager, then, to use one Eucharist». «μία γὰρ σὰρξ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἓν ποτήριον εἰς ἕνωσιν τοῦ αἵματος αὐτοῦ, ἓν θυσιαστήριον, ὡς εἷς ἐπίσκοπος ἅμα τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ καὶ διακόνοις τοῖς συνδούλοις μου» is kept in full: A «the flesh of our Lord Jesus Christ is one, and the cup for union with his blood is one, the altar is one, as the bishop is one together with the presbytery and the deacons who are my fellow slaves»; B «one flesh of our Lord Jesus Christ, and one cup for union with his blood… one altar, just as there is one bishop, with the presbytery and the deacons, my fellow slaves». «ἵνα, ὃ ἐὰν πράσσητε, κατὰ θεὸν πράσσητε» remains purpose, not a wish: A «in order that whatever you may do, you may do according to God»; B «so that whatever you do, you do it God's way» (disclosed reading equivalent; fronting does not reverse γάρ or ἵνα). No negation invented; no wrong inline citation (1 Cor recall only noted). Title names the thought.

Source paragraph 1: Greek text matches Ignatius Philadelphians 4 locus. Pass A gloss renders 'Σπουδάσατε οὖν μιᾷ εὐχαριστίᾳ χρῆσθαι' as 'Therefore be diligent to make use of a single Eucharist', preserving sense and agency. Pass B: 'Be eager, then, to use one Eucharist' matches Greek σπουδάσατε and μιᾷ εὐχαριστίᾳ χρῆσθαι; 'so that whatever you do, you do it God's way' corresponds to ἵνα, ὃ ἐὰν πράσσητε, κατὰ θεὸν πράσσητε. Completeness: all clauses covered—no omissions of 'μία γὰρ σὰρξ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἓν ποτήριον εἰς ἕνωσιν τοῦ αἵματος αὐτοῦ, ἓν θυσιαστήριον, ὡς εἷς ἐπίσκοπος ἅμα τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ καὶ διακόνοις τοῖς συνδούλοις μου'. Negation: none present. Agency: 'whatever you may do' (πράσσητε) preserved in both Pass A/B. Modality: 'be diligent' (σπουδάσατε) → 'be eager' (Pass B) acceptable; 'you may do' (πράσσητε) → 'you do it' (Pass B) preserves voluntariness. Doctrine: unity of flesh, cup, altar, bishop/presbytery/deacons maintained. Scripture: Notes correctly state 1 Corinthians 10:16-17 is not inline; no false citation added. Title 'One Eucharist, One Altar' names the thought. No uncertainties; all checks passed.
